note_tweet.text:
Meta Muse. It built a tracker from scratch to my specifications where I could record each item I needed, how many units I needed, how many units are in a pack, and how many packs I needed, along with any notes I needed to keep on it.

And then each item's record had child records to track how many had been ordered and when, how many had been delivered when, and if any needed to be returned/refunded. There was also a simple dashboard to show overall how much was needed, ordered, delivered, and outstanding by item, pack, and unit, along with a text search so I could quickly pull up any item.

The many-to-one relationships between the item records and their associated ordering and delivery records was the big advantage over the flat spreadsheet I've used in previous years. Made it really easy to see exactly what was happening with each item. Plus, having it right on my phone with phone-friendly forms was a huge upgrade for me.
